status: Owner accepted texture direction; oversized clumps removed and final native review passed. Not a complete cliff/overhang system.
owner_direction: Mostly better texturing, subtle shape changes. AC3 Frontier and vanilla Skyrim are references; Skyrim example not a prescription for Grand Canyon geography.

primary_sources.note: Original publisher screenshots, not texture mods.

primary_sources.authors: Joel Burgess and Nathan Purkeypile; Bethesda/GDC2013
primary_sources.note: Primary developer account of modular art/level design; no specific cliff shader implementation claimed.
Publisher art context; AC3 remains a visual target, not a copied asset source.

visual_inferences: Use coherent stone colour across the wall and supporting rock meshes.
Readable broad fractures and restrained fine grain; avoid exaggerated noisy normals.
Keep large shapes and silhouettes composed; add only small real ledges as needed.
Texture detail is not a replacement for real climbable holds later.
test: Material-only; core geometry exactly ffa926b0/963bbd03. Retained generated master colour, shared wall/model coordinates and8m scale, normal relief reduced.
asset_rights: References are for analysis only. Game assets remain our generated masters and previously approved CC0 source geometry.
owner_feedback: Close rock texture looks quite good; large clump rocks look unrealistic and obviously scattered.
current_direction: Keep approved generated material. No oversized synthetic cliff masses and no cellular terrain carving. Ordinary rocks remain.

retired_scatter.scope: Both sides of three canyon reaches; component assertions, not frame-rate measurements.

retired_distance_fade.reason: Excessively flattened the wider wall; the repeated large facets belonged to retired geometry, so the strong colour fade was inappropriate.
